title: Coalitions Deliver Progress at COP31 as Consensus Frays
gist: COP31 in Antalya failed to reach consensus on fossil fuels and finance (the Antalya Pact was rejected by ~90 countries), but voluntary coalitions delivered, notably a 75+ country pledge (incl. China) to lift electricity's share of final energy from 23% to 35% by 2035 backed by $156bn/yr of utility grid, renewables and storage plans. Data-center demand (~945 TWh by 2030) and a $330bn energy-import shock after strikes on Iran sharpen the economic case, and BCG urges businesses to implement now and build policy capabilities ahead of COP32.

insights.claim: At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, negotiators failed to reach consensus on core issues such as fossil fuels and climate finance, and the main political decision, the Antalya Pact, was rejected by around ninety countries.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Multilateral climate policy is fragmenting; do not underwrite transition investments on the assumption of a binding global fossil-fuel phase-down.
insights.quote: was rejected by around ninety countries
insights.locator: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya

insights.claim: BCG argues formal negotiations and voluntary coalitions are complementary tracks: coalitions move faster but depend on negotiations to set direction, while a vibrant Action Agenda can help get stalled negotiations back on track.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Track coalition-level pledges (sector, utility, country clubs) as the leading indicator of real transition capex rather than headline COP text.
insights.quote: Coalitions can move faster, but they depend on the negotiations to set the direction and bring everyone along.

insights.claim: More than 75 countries, including China, backed a voluntary COP31 pledge to raise electricity's share of final energy consumption from 23% today to 35% by 2035, even as negotiators argued over whether the goal should be explicitly tied to clean energy.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 12-point rise in electricity's share of final energy in ~9 years implies sustained demand growth for grids, power equipment, and generation regardless of fuel mix.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, electrification showed what coalitions can achieve

insights.claim: The COP31 electrification pledge was paired with utilities' plans to invest at least $156 billion a year in grids, renewables and storage, showing coalitions can attach financing and infrastructure commitments to high-level targets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: $156bn/yr of committed utility capex is a direct demand signal for transmission, transformer, storage and renewables supply chains.
insights.quote: at least $156 billion a year in grids, renewables and storage

insights.claim: COP31's electrification package included nearly $95 million in catalytic finance aiming to mobilize more than $1.2 billion of private investment, plus a new IEA-led mechanism to track progress ahead of COP32.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Blended-finance leverage of roughly 13x is targeted; an IEA tracking mechanism creates a public scorecard to monitor pledge delivery.

themes.theme: Other coalition outcomes under the GCAA

insights.claim: Under the Global Climate Action Agenda at COP31, philanthropies announced $480 million for methane and other super pollutants, regenerative agriculture programs reached 66 million hectares, and the coalition on compliance carbon markets grew to 13 members.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Methane abatement and compliance carbon-market linkage are where voluntary coalitions are gaining scale; watch for carbon-market interoperability and methane-monitoring demand.
insights.locator: New efforts under the GCAA included

insights.claim: New COP31 initiatives included a Global Zero Waste Alliance and a UNIDO-hosted green industrialization agenda, while Brazil presented the deforestation roadmap called for by 93 countries at COP30.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Green industrialization and deforestation policy are moving via coalitions; relevant for emerging-market industrial and agri/forestry exposures.
insights.locator: New efforts under the GCAA included

themes.theme: Energy security and AI power demand

insights.claim: According to the IEA, data center electricity consumption is set to more than double to around 945 TWh by 2030, strengthening the economic case for electrification and grid investment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI/data-center load growth reinforces the grid and generation capex cycle independent of climate politics.
insights.quote: Data center electricity consumption is set to more than double to around 945 TWh by 2030
insights.locator: It also comes at a time when the energy transition

insights.claim: Fossil fuel importers paid an estimated gross extra cost of $330 billion for seaborne crude, oil products and LNG in the six months after the strikes on Iran, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, highlighting energy-security exposure as a driver of transition.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
entities: Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air
insights.so_what: Import-dependent economies have a security (not just climate) motive to electrify; supports domestic renewables and grid policy in fuel-importing nations.
insights.quote: a gross extra cost of $330 billion

insights.claim: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, a strong El Niño could make 2027 hotter still, and the UN says exceeding 1.5°C of warming is now inevitable, shifting focus to limiting overshoot.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Physical climate risk is rising near term; adaptation, resilience and weather-exposed sectors (agriculture, insurance, utilities) warrant closer scrutiny.
insights.quote: it is now inevitable that the world will exceed 1.5°C of global warming
insights.locator: COP31’s Summit came during a year

insights.claim: BCG says progress requires strong, coherent carbon pricing aligned with national decarbonization goals, effective concessional finance for emerging nations, and investment in infrastructure such as electricity grids.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Carbon-price coherence and concessional finance are the policy gaps to watch; their absence caps emerging-market transition capex.
insights.locator: However, the work ahead is significant

insights.claim: Ahead of COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia in November 2027, BCG advises businesses to implement COP31 pledges (e.g., contributing to national electrification programs), help shape regulation via coalitions, and engage with the global stocktake.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: COP32 is the next catalyst date for climate-policy-sensitive assets; corporate engagement in national electrification programs is the near-term channel.

insights.claim: BCG argues that amid increased policy volatility and fragmentation, enhanced policy capabilities can be a source of competitive advantage for proactive companies that assess climate risks to operations and invest to reduce vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Favor companies with strong regulatory/policy engagement and explicit climate-vulnerability planning as fragmentation rises.
insights.quote: Enhanced policy capabilities can be a source of competitive advantage for companies who are proactive
insights.locator: Businesses should also take a careful look
